2. The material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule are that the Opposite Party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted pre-emption case No.65 of 1997 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Narail stating, inter-alia, that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer to the case jote by inheritance as well as by purchase while the pre-emptee is a stranger, who purchased the case land from his father by a registered kabala dated 14.12.1995 at the consideration of Tk. 12,000/-. It has been further asserted that his father Afsaruddin earlier gifted the case land verbally to him and after the death of Afsaruddin the pre-emptor came to learnt that his father has already been transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner. No notice of the said transfer in question was served upon the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 and hence the case on making the statutory deposit. 

 18. Be that as it may, provisions for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is not applicable to a transfer in favour of a co-sharer whose interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance. In this case the transfer under the kabala dated 14.12.1995 was made to this petitioner by his father is protected and immune from the pre-emption under sub-section 10(a) to section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act inasmuch as the pre-emptee's interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance simply because the pre-emptee inherited his father's share.
